title: iter-4 bit-127 mask makes inline-vs-decoder duplication WORSE, not better
description: iter-3 R4-001 flagged the inline price math at dataLayer.ts as duplicating decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice in marketStats.ts. iter-4's CR-2 fix (the bit-127 mask) addressed correctness — production now decodes ask prices correctly — but did so by introducing a THIRD bit-decode formula `(BigInt(x) & ((1n<<127n)-1n)) >> 64n` that is neither decodeAskPrice (`id & (ASK_BIT_OFFSET - 1n) / PRICE_BIT_OFFSET`) nor decodeBidPrice (`U64_MAX - (id / PRICE_BIT_OFFSET)`). The inline comment block (lines 204-218) explicitly notes that decodeBidPrice in marketStats.ts uses an inverted formula that is correct only for test fixtures — confirming that two formulas now coexist for bids, with the inline one taking the production path and the marketStats one taking the test path. Three bit-decode sites, three different formulas, one shared concept. The iter-3 finding's recommendation (delete the inline, route through a shared decoder) was not actioned; instead the inline grew from 7 lines to 27 lines (try/catch/comment expansion).
impact: Triple-source-of-truth for price decoding. A future re-capture of chain-shape.md that adjusts the encoding (e.g. discovering a different ask flag layout, or finding the inversion is conditional on something) requires coordinated edits in three places, with two of them being private functions that are not on the production read path. The marketStats decoders now exist in production source as test-only code paths (R4-003 below). The inline decoder at lines 219-245 is the only formula production ever sees, but it is the LEAST visible and LEAST documented of the three (no JSDoc, no exported name, no test-fixture round-trip).
recommendation: Move the bit-127 decoder to a shared module (e.g. priceDecode.ts exporting `decodePriceFromOrderId(orderId: string): number | undefined`). Have decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice in marketStats.ts call it. Then the inline at dataLayer.ts becomes `price: decodePriceFromOrderId(orderIdStr)` — one line, one source of truth. Tests that build fixtures via the bid-inversion encoding still pass because the new shared decoder applies the bit-127 mask uniformly (which the iter-4 comment already confirms `Holds for both bids and asks`).

title: iter-3 R4-002 still applies — LOC now 1257 (was 1225 in iter-3), still ~4-6x spec envelope
description: wc -l on the same file set as iter-3 reports 1257 total — iter-4 added 32 more LOC despite the synthesis claim that 'iter-4 mostly removed lines.' Net effect: removed unused imports (~3 lines saved), removed unused param (~1 line saved), but added the bit-127 mask comment block (~12 lines), the console.warn elaboration (~10 lines), and the buildDeps factory comment block (~5 lines). dataLayer.ts grew from 427 to 461 lines (+34). Spec envelope remains 200-300 for a single-route read-only SPA. Iter-4 demonstrates the same pattern iter-3 did: a precisely-scoped refactor (one-bit mask change + one closure refactor) ends up growing the file because each new concern has to be threaded through the monolith. The iter-2 R4-001 split recommendation (rpc.ts / poolReader.ts / eventReader.ts / composer) was not actioned in iter-3 OR iter-4.
impact: LOC trend: iter-1 ~1100 → iter-2 1211 → iter-3 1225 → iter-4 1257. Three iterations, +147 LOC, zero structural decomposition. Each iteration's narrow fix grows the same file. Without a split, cycle-2 onwards will continue stretching dataLayer.ts. The synthesis-notes.md claim that 'iter-4 mostly removed lines' is empirically false — net delta is +32.
recommendation: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-001/R4-002. Either (a) split dataLayer.ts now (suggested four files: rpc.ts for the JsonRpcEnvelope+rpc helper, poolReader.ts for resolvePoolInnerFields/traverseBigVector/buildPoolInnerState, eventReader.ts for buildQueryEventsFn + RawFillEvent mapping, composer.ts for fetchPoolStats + runDataLayer), or (b) get an explicit sign-off in the consolidated review acknowledging the LOC overshoot is permanent and capping the budget at 1257 going forward.
evidence:
$ wc -l src/*.ts src/*.tsx src/components/*.tsx vite.config.ts
  461 src/dataLayer.ts
  ...
 1257 total
# iter-3: 1225, iter-2: 1211. Net +46 across two iterations of 'narrow fix' patches.

title: iter-3 R4-003 still applies — decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice now strictly dead-on-prod, retained only for test fixtures
description: iter-3 R4-003 flagged that with traverseBigVector now populating Order.price, the `o.price !== undefined ? o.price : decode...` ternary in computeMarketStats never takes the false branch in production. iter-4 did not change this — both decoders are still defined, both ternaries still present. The marketStats.ts comment at lines 53-54 even now says 'For bids, the order_id decode is tautologically correct against test fixtures but wrong against real chain order_ids' — explicitly admitting the function exists in production source for a tests-only purpose. The iter-4 dataLayer.ts comment at line 211-213 reinforces this: 'decodeBidPrice in marketStats.ts uses the inverted formula and remains correct only for the test fixtures that mirror it'. The codebase now contains a self-acknowledged test-fixture-only function in production source.
impact: Same as iter-3 R4-003: ~25 LOC of bit-math production source that production runtime never executes. Now compounded by R4-001: iter-4's explicit comments call out the test-only nature of decodeBidPrice, making the unjustified placement glaring. Hidden test coupling — a future maintainer who deletes the `decodeBidPrice` line breaks no production path but breaks ~6 test cases (a textbook smell). The fix is the same as iter-3 R4-003: move to tests/_fixtures.ts or similar.
recommendation: Same as iter-3 R4-003. Move decodeAskPrice and decodeBidPrice into tests/_fixtures.ts; require Order.price to always be present at the marketStats.ts boundary (typed as `price: number` not `price?: number`). Test fixtures explicitly compute price via the test-side helper, which is honest about what's a test concern. Combined with R4-001 (single shared bit-127 decoder), this produces one production decoder + one inverted-formula test helper, instead of three competing decoders.

title: iter-4 buildDeps() factory in main.tsx is a real improvement — closes iter-3 R4-004
description: iter-3 R4-004 flagged the `let cachedPackageId = ''; const _origLoadManifest = deps.loadManifest; deps.loadManifest = ...` mutation trick as a closure-over-let smell. iter-4 replaced it with a `buildDeps()` factory that captures `let packageId: string | undefined` in a single closure shared between loadManifest (writer) and fetchPoolStats (reader). The mutation is gone, the closure is local to the factory, and there is now an explicit guard (`if (packageId === undefined) throw ...`) that turns the previous silent-empty-string failure mode into an actionable wiring error. The factory is also testable in isolation if needed (return value is the AppDeps object). Module-level state is now zero. This is a clean fix.
impact: Positive — the iter-3 high finding is closed by this change. The closure-over-let pattern is still present (packageId captured by both functions) but it is now (a) initialized to undefined explicitly, (b) read with an undefined-check that throws a named error, (c) scoped to a single factory call, and (d) commented to explain the load-order requirement. None of the iter-3 hazards remain.
recommendation: No action — flagging as info to credit the fix. The ONE residual nit is that the load-order invariant ('loadManifest MUST run before fetchPoolStats') is enforced at runtime via the throw rather than by the type system. A follow-up could move the packageId into a parameter on fetchPoolStats and have App.tsx thread the LoadedManifest from the loadManifest result, removing the closure entirely — but this requires touching App.tsx's deps interface and is out of scope for the current carry-forward set.

title: iter-2/iter-3 R4-005 still applies — types.ts still exports 5 unused interfaces
description: iter-4 did not touch types.ts. ManifestPoolEntry, DeploymentManifest, BigVectorMeta, RawFillEntry, RawOrderInfoEvent are still defined but their only references across src/ are inside types.ts itself. Zero importers in src/components, src/App.tsx, src/dataLayer.ts, src/main.tsx, or src/manifest.ts. Verified via `grep -rn` on src/. PoolCardData is still declared in components/PoolCard.tsx, contradicting types.ts's file-header claim of being the home for it. The iter-4 patches in dataLayer.ts are the canonical example of where these would have been useful: the buildQueryEventsFn parsedJson at dataLayer.ts:328-345 is still stringly-typed (`String(j['pool_id'] ?? '')`, `Number(j['timestamp'] ?? ev.timestampMs ?? 0)`), exactly the shape that RawOrderInfoEvent in types.ts already names.
impact: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-005. The single-source-of-truth narrative the file's doc comment promises is false. ~50 LOC of visual noise. iter-4's CR-2 patch lived inside the very function (traverseBigVector) that should have been consuming these types — the bit-127 decode operates on `String(orderFields['order_id'] ?? keys[i] ?? '0')`, where `orderFields` is `Record<string, unknown>` and a typed Order interface with the chain-shape would have made the cast tree-shakable. iter-4 did NOT clean up unused imports comprehensively (synthesis claims removal of LoadedManifest/Book from dataLayer, but the dead exports themselves were not addressed).
recommendation: Same as iter-2/iter-3. Either delete the 5 unused interfaces or actually use them. Quickest action: import RawOrderInfoEvent into dataLayer.ts and type the buildQueryEventsFn body's `j` as `RawOrderInfoEvent` (with a cast at the parsedJson boundary). That would eliminate ~6 of the `String(j[...] ?? '...')` stringly-typed extractions. Same for RunDataLayerArgs.manifest → DeploymentManifest (closes iter-3 R4-011 too).

title: iter-2/iter-3 R4-006 still applies — runDataLayer + fetchSinglePoolStats parallel APIs unchanged
description: iter-4 did not touch the public-API surface. Both `runDataLayer` (test-only — tests/networkShape.test.ts:139 is the sole importer) and `fetchSinglePoolStats` (prod-only — main.tsx:23 is the sole importer) are still exported. runDataLayer keeps its own Promise.allSettled + sentinel-card construction, parallel to App.tsx's two effects. iter-4's bit-127 mask lives inside fetchPoolStats so runDataLayer indirectly inherits it (the only reason networkShape.test.ts kept passing across iterations) — but the orchestration logic remains duplicated across three sites. The synthesis-notes.md iter-4 section does not mention this; it was a iter-3 carry-forward and remains a iter-4 carry-forward.
impact: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-006. Three sites maintain near-identical sentinel/error/orchestration logic. iter-4's CR-2 fix was vertical (bit math), iter-4's main.tsx refactor was horizontal (closure shape) — neither touched orchestration, which is exactly where collapsing the three sites would help. Test-only runDataLayer remains a tautology risk: networkShape.test.ts could pass even if App.tsx orchestration broke.
recommendation: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-006. Pick one orchestrator. Option (a) — delete fetchSinglePoolStats and have App.tsx call runDataLayer once per refresh cycle — would also collapse R4-007 (App.tsx duplication). Option (b) — extract the per-pool sentinel-card construction into a small helper, called from both runDataLayer and App.tsx's two effects.

title: iter-2/iter-3 R4-007 still applies — App.tsx still duplicates ~30 LOC across two effects
description: iter-4 did not touch App.tsx. The initial-load effect (lines 44-82) and the periodic-refresh effect (lines 91-125) still both inline the same Promise.allSettled + sentinel-card map + filter+map for poolErrors + setState. ~30 LOC duplicated, byte-for-byte identical except the initial-load effect uses `manifest.pools` and the refresh effect uses `manifestPoolsRef.current`. The synthesis-notes.md does not mention this — it was a iter-3 carry-forward and remains a iter-4 carry-forward.
impact: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-007. A future cycle that adjusts sentinel-card shape (e.g. to add a 'lastUpdatedMs' field for the 30s freshness AC, or to add a 'refreshCount' for debug instrumentation) will have to update both effects independently and they will silently diverge. The iter-4 CR-2 patch is irrelevant to this finding, but the unfixed duplication compounds with R4-006 — three orchestration sites now (runDataLayer + 2 in App.tsx).
recommendation: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-007. Extract `async function refreshCards(pools, deps): Promise<{cards, poolErrors}>` and call it from both effects. Or collapse to a single effect with a guarded setInterval that runs immediately on mount.

title: iter-4 console.warn additions are heavier than the conceptual change deserves
description: iter-3's price-injection block was 7 lines (per iter-3 R4-008). iter-4's version is 27 lines: declaration + ASK_FLAG_MASK constant + try + BigInt-mask-shift + finite-check + 4-line console.warn + undefined-assign + catch + 4-line console.warn + undefined-assign + close-brace. The conceptual change from iter-3 was 'add a mask before the shift' (~1 line of math) plus 'log instead of swallow' (~2 lines per branch). The actual iter-4 patch grew the block by ~20 lines. The two console.warn calls have nearly identical structure (formatted error message + 'falling back to compute-time order_id decode' tail) and could be a 2-line helper called from both branches. The ASK_FLAG_MASK constant is computed inside the function on every iteration of the for-loop instead of being module-scoped.
impact: Tiny. Reading cost only. The reading cost is real, though — the entire 27-line block sits inside a nested for-loop inside an async function inside a 461-line module, and the bulk of the block is logging boilerplate, not the actual work. Combined with R4-001 (the math should be a function call) and R4-005 (the field extraction should be typed), the cleaner shape is a single line: `price: decodePriceFromOrderId(orderIdStr)`. The current shape is a 27-line block doing what should be a one-liner property assignment + a shared logging helper.
recommendation: Move ASK_FLAG_MASK to module scope (it is a constant). Extract the logging into a small helper: `function decodePrice(orderIdStr: string): number | undefined { try { ... } catch (err) { console.warn(...); return undefined; } }` — then the call site is `price: decodePrice(orderIdStr)`. Even better, combine with R4-001's recommendation and put it in priceDecode.ts shared with marketStats.ts.

title: iter-4 doc comment in dataLayer.ts:204-218 is now LONGER than the iter-3 comment it replaced
description: iter-3 R4-009 flagged a 5-line comment block as 'longer than the code it documents'. iter-4 grew that comment to 15 lines (lines 204-218), now describing: the empirical capture of two order_ids with their numeric values, an explanation of the bit-127 ask flag, an explicit contradiction of chain-shape.md's prose ('the chain-shape prose's inverted for bids claim is contradicted by the captured data'), an admission that decodeBidPrice in marketStats.ts is fixture-only, and a justification for the bit-127 mask working for both sides. The comment is honest and well-researched, but it's also a 15-line essay sitting inside a 27-line code block (R4-008) inside a nested loop. The volume signals that the author isn't sure the encoding is settled — which is correctness territory, not simplicity territory, but the simplicity cost is the visual weight.
impact: Low. The comment is informative and accurate (matches captured chain data per the synthesis notes). But its placement at the call site rather than at a decoder definition site means the next maintainer reads it inline every time they touch traverseBigVector, even if their change has nothing to do with price decoding. If extracted to priceDecode.ts (per R4-001), the comment lives next to the decoder where it belongs.
recommendation: Trim the inline comment at lines 204-218 to a single sentence + cross-reference: `// Decode price per priceDecode.ts (mask bit 127, then take high 64). See decoder for chain-shape.md captured-id rationale.` Move the 15-line essay into a JSDoc above the decoder function in the new priceDecode.ts module.

title: iter-2/iter-3 R4-010 still applies — RawFillEvent and FillRecord still structurally identical
description: iter-4 did not touch fetchPoolStats's fill-records mapping. The mapping at dataLayer.ts:397-402 is still a field-for-field copy from RawFillEvent (fillFetcher.ts:19-24) to FillRecord (fillAggregator.ts:9-14). Both interfaces have the same four fields (poolId, timestampMs, baseQuantity, price) with the same types. Unchanged from iter-2/iter-3.
impact: Same as iter-2/iter-3 — pure noise + drift hazard if the shapes diverge. iter-4's bit-127 mask had nothing to do with this and didn't address it.
recommendation: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-010. Pick one type or have fillFetcher return FillRecord[] directly.

title: iter-2/iter-3 R4-011 still applies — module-level rpcId and inline RunDataLayerArgs.manifest unchanged
description: iter-4 did not touch the module-level `let rpcId = 0` (line 43) or the inline `manifest: { network?; packages?; pools? }` shape on RunDataLayerArgs (lines 26-34). Both iter-2/iter-3 findings still apply byte-for-byte. The inline manifest shape is a particularly clean fix opportunity — types.ts already exports DeploymentManifest with exactly this shape (R4-005), so replacing the inline shape with `manifest: DeploymentManifest` would simultaneously close R4-011 and convert one of the five dead types.ts exports into a live one (chipping at R4-005).
impact: Carry-forward, no new harm. Flagging so consolidator does not lose track. Combining the fix with R4-005 turns two findings into one ~3-line edit (import DeploymentManifest from './types.js' + replace the inline shape).
recommendation: Same as iter-2/iter-3 R4-011. Scope rpcId inside runDataLayer (or set id:1 since each rpc call is independent on the wire) and import DeploymentManifest from types.ts to replace the inline shape.

title: iter-4 cleanup of unused imports/params is real but small in absolute terms
description: Crediting what iter-4 got right from a simplicity lens: removed unused `import * as React` from main.tsx (the file uses createRoot directly, no JSX needs the React import in modern react-jsx mode); removed unused `LoadedManifest`/`Book` imports from dataLayer.ts (per synthesis); removed unused `poolId` param from buildQueryEventsFn signature with a comment explaining the downstream filter. These are real wins — each removed item shrinks the API surface. Net LOC effect is small (~3-5 lines saved) and is overshadowed by the +32 LOC from R4-002, but they are directionally correct simplicity work.
impact: None — informational. Helps the consolidator see iter-4 made some genuine simplicity progress (alongside R4-004 buildDeps fix) even though the headline LOC went up.
recommendation: No action. Continue removing unused imports/params in future cycles — same direction. Pair with the R4-005 fix (use DeploymentManifest from types.ts) for the next opportunity to actually shrink files instead of adding constants.
evidence: src/main.tsx:20-23 — no `import * as React` (was present in iter-3); src/dataLayer.ts:19-24 — no LoadedManifest or Book in the import list; src/dataLayer.ts:312 — buildQueryEventsFn signature is `(rpcUrl, packageId)` not `(rpcUrl, packageId, poolId)`.
